attempts.summary: Installed AIDE on node1, initialized a file-integrity baseline database covering /etc using the distro-default AlmaLinux 9 aide.conf ruleset (specific NORMAL/CONTENT rules for sensitive files like /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/sudoers, plus a recursive '/etc PERMS' catch-all), activated it as the live database (aide.db.gz), and validated detection by intentionally modifying /etc/hosts and removing /etc/motd, confirming AIDE flagged both, then restoring state and re-initializing a clean baseline. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and AIDE db checksum baseline, issued a native reboot, confirmed the connection dropped and later recovered, verified boot_id changed (4a743885... -> f4ea82c9...), and confirmed the AIDE database and clean-check status survived the restart unchanged.
